query: USMCA joint review July 1 2026 outcome - did US provide written notice of withdrawal under Article 34.6? Latest news on Trump USMCA withdrawal or renewal decision June-July 2026
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's the bottom line:

**No, the United States did NOT provide written notice of withdrawal under Article 34.6.** At the July 1, 2026 six-year joint review (conducted under the separate **Article 34.7** mechanism), the US instead **declined to agree to the 16-year extension**. USTR Ambassador Greer stated the US "did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form," but confirmed the agreement "remains in force."

Key distinction the sources confirm explicitly:
- **Article 34.7** (what happened): non-extension triggers **annual joint reviews** each year through the scheduled July 1, 2036 expiration; agreement stays fully in force.
- **Article 34.6** (what did NOT happen): withdrawal requires written notice effective 6 months later — no such notice was issued, no withdrawal clock started.

Canada and Mexico both supported the 16-year extension; only the US declined. Bilateral US–Mexico talks were set for the week of July 20, 2026. Analysts frame this as prolonged uncertainty rather than termination.

key_facts: The US did NOT provide written notice of withdrawal under Article 34.6; instead it declined to extend under Article 34.7 at the July 1, 2026 joint review.
USTR Ambassador Jamieson Greer stated: 'The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. As a result, the USMCA is not renewed,' but that it 'remains in force.'
Canada and Mexico both supported extending the agreement for an additional 16-year term; only the US declined, so no consensus for extension was reached.
Non-extension triggers an annual joint review cycle under Article 34.7.4, recurring each year until extension is agreed or the agreement expires on July 1, 2036.
The USMCA remains fully in force; no trade rules, tariffs, or rules of origin changed as a result of the decision.
Article 34.6 withdrawal requires written notice effective six months after delivery; no such notice was issued and no withdrawal clock has begun.
The 16-year extension remains available at any time via written confirmation by all three heads of government.
A third round of US-Mexico bilateral negotiations was scheduled for the week of July 20, 2026, in Mexico City.
Analysts (CSIS, White & Case, Brookings) describe the outcome as 'prolonged uncertainty' that could stall North American investment rather than an immediate rupture.
